Subject: Nightwatch: p95 spike 00:45-01:05 — QuickCart impact

Team —

Monitoring alerted at ~00:46 PDT for a p95 jump on the gen-api surface serving QuickCart (us-west region). Short summary:
- Window: 00:45–01:05 PDT
- Symptom: p95 increased from ~480ms to ~3.8s on /v1/generate (streaming off for many calls), overall QPS for QuickCart down ~30% vs baseline
- Affected model path: primary model variant open-llama-13b/v2 (hosted) — we saw automatic fallback to open-llama-13b-q4 (quant) for some requests but not consistently
- Cache signals: KV cache hit-rate for QuickCart routes dropped from 86% → 32% during window
- Autoscaler: no large pod churn in metrics; small spike in kernel preempt logs

Attachments: metrics-snapshot-20260929.png, kv-warmup-timeline-20260929.csv (small extracts attached). JIRA: RINF-3421 created.

Immediate asks:
1) SRE/Eng (karthik) — short RCA sketch and recommended immediate mitigations (we need a low-risk change we can apply without rolling all customers).
2) Product (marissa) — tradeoff guidance: do we (a) enable protective-routing to QuickCart-dedicated pool, (b) temporarily pin QuickCart to the quantized variant as primary, or (c) increase KV cache TTL / sticky warmstart? Provide cost/quality callouts for each.
3) Sales/AE (ben) — hold on external comms until we have a one-paragraph customer note to send to ops@quickcart.com. We should avoid floods; prefer a calm, technical note with timeline + mitigations.

I'll keep the thread open — please reply inline.

— Lauren

Subject: Re: Nightwatch: p95 spike 00:45-01:05 — QuickCart impact

Lauren — thanks for the alert and artifacts. Quick, high-confidence observations from the infra side after looking at node traces and the profiler:

1) Root signal: abrupt KV cache "evaporation" for QuickCart routes. We saw many cold KV misses between 00:44–00:59 that aligns with the p95 window. The warmup estimator didn't kick in fast enough because of a recent orchestration tweak that reduced sticky warmstart windows for short-lived instances (we rolled that change last week to reduce memory pressure).

2) Secondary: a small number (4) of inference workers hit long tail kernel-preempt cycles when switching from warm to cold contexts; this amplified latencies for streaming responses. Not seeing a disk or network saturation issue.

3) Why fallback behavior was inconsistent: fallback to quant variant requires KV entries for model routing; when KV misses spike, routing can bounce between variants and produce both higher latency and variable QPS.

Immediate mitigations (risk/cost):
- LOW RISK: Re-enable sticky warmstart for QuickCart route only (config change). Effect: should reduce cold starts and restore KV hit-rate within 5–8 minutes. No infra restart required.
- MED RISK: Increase KV cache TTL for QuickCart and trigger a manual warmup job for the route. Effect: faster steady-state but requires background warmup traffic (we can run synthetic warmers).
- HIGH RISK: Force-pin QuickCart to q4 quantized variant. Effect: reduces latency variability and CPU work, but may reduce generation quality; needs product approval.
- RISKY OP: Rolling restart of 4 affected workers to flush odd kernel state — short disruption possible; prefer this only if warmstart toggle isn't effective.

I recommend LOW RISK (re-enable sticky warmstart for this route) now, and then run the manual warmup to rebuild KV entries over the next 20–30 minutes. If that fails, pin to quant as fallback. I'll prepare the toggle and the warmup job; need Product signoff on pin-to-quant option as fallback.

I'll open a short-run deployment PR and can flip the sticky flag within 10 minutes after approval.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
SRE Lead — Inference Platform
Redwood Inference

Thanks Karthik — that aligns with what I was worried about. A few product-level notes and asks:

- Priority: minimize customer-visible quality regressions. QuickCart has highly extractive prompts where quantization might have a non-trivial risk; we need an A/B test if we were to switch them to q4 as primary. So pin-to-quant is a last-resort fallback.
- Preferred short-term: do sticky warmstart + manual warmup as Karthik suggests. That should get KV hit-rate back and be lowest-risk.
- Questions we need answers to quickly:
  1) ETA and cost delta for running the manual warmup job for QuickCart for 60 minutes (estimate compute cost and token units).
  2) Approx measured quality delta between open-llama-13b/v2 and the q4 variant on QuickCart's most common prompt set (we have an internal eval harness we could run — can the ML team run a quick pass?)

I drafted a short customer note below (feel free to edit) — Ben, if you can hold until we confirm the warmstart toggle and then send, that'd be ideal.
